decisions.statement: A call naming no argument reads the past twenty-four hours.
A run is one test file run on its own.
The rows are read from beside the page whose code that test proves.
A test file beside no page of its own is gathered under the page it proves.
Every entries file the tree holds is read rather than the files beside one kind.
A folder git or a package manager owns is walked past.
Every numbered file of those rows is read rather than the first alone.
A row naming the test phase is read and no other row is.
A landing writes such a row and an audit writes one too.
Both are read here.
The runs are gathered under the test file that ran.
A test run's processor time is what the run spawned spent rather than the measuring run's own.
A test file may spend five processor seconds and a change carrying one past that is refused.
A test file is throttled at five hundred and twelve megabytes rather than ended.
The memory reported is what the run peaked at under that throttle.
A file that would not read is named rather than counting as no runs.
A row a write left half appended is passed over and the rest of the file read.
A test file holding no run of what was chosen is not listed at all.
The total counts the distinct runs read rather than the records read.
The total shares the processor time over the distinct runs read.
The total draws its average memory as `-`.
A run that noted no high-water mark is left out of the memory reported.
Test files are ordered by what their runs took on average.
Test files taking equal processor time are ordered by name.
A run writes no value the commit has.
Nothing here runs a test.
An argument this command does not take is refused.
Every test file is drawn with the one ceiling every test file is held to.

definition: the command saying what a test run cost in processor time and memory
